related.name: Audio Dynamic Range & Data Rate Calculator

guidance: The volume is net internal air, after the driver, bracing, lining and any tube are taken out; loose filling can add up to about 40 % to the effective volume, while a stuffed box tunes differently again. Thiele/Small figures are small-signal averages with real tolerances (Fs around 15 %, Vas 20-30 %), so treat the volume as a starting point and measure the finished system. This page computes an alignment, not a loudspeaker: it does not choose a driver, model excursion or power handling, or design a crossover.
method: A sealed box adds an air spring behind the cone. In the lumped Thiele/Small model the box compliance sits in parallel with the driver's suspension, so the stiffening factor is the same for the system Q and the resonance: Qtc = Qts x sqrt(1 + Vas/Vb) and Fc = Fs x sqrt(1 + Vas/Vb), where Vas is the volume of air with the driver's own compliance and Vb is the net box volume. Solving the Q relation for the box gives Vb = Vas / ((Qtc/Qts)^2 - 1), which is why a target only a little above Qts asks for an enormous box, and why no sealed box can pull the system Q below the driver's Qts: the air spring only ever adds stiffness, so Qtc >= Qts and Vb -> infinity as Qtc -> Qts. The page works in both directions, from a target Qtc to the volume and from a volume to the Qtc, and both paths share one ratio, Vas/Vb, which is also reported with the box size in Vas units. The response is a second-order high-pass, |H| = f^2 / sqrt((f^2 - Fc^2)^2 + (f x Fc / Qtc)^2), so the level at Fc is exactly 20 log10(Qtc) dB, the -3 dB point solves the same expression for half power, F3 = Fc x sqrt(u + sqrt(u^2 + 1)) with u = 1/(2 Qtc^2) - 1, and a peak appears only above Qtc = 1/sqrt(2), at Fc / sqrt(1 - 1/(2 Qtc^2)) and 20 log10(Qtc / sqrt(1 - 1/(4 Qtc^2))) dB. Because that peak is a ripple rather than a bump just above the Butterworth Q, the page reports one only from 0.1 dB (about Qtc 0.77) and otherwise says the response is flat into the roll-off. Above the box the response is flat and below it the slope is 12 dB per octave, half the 24 dB of a ported box. Typical targets are 0.5 (well damped, large box), 0.577 (Bessel, best group delay), 0.707 (maximally flat, F3 = Fc) and 0.9 to 1.2 (smaller boxes with a rising peak). Inputs are 5-500 Hz of Fs, 0.05-2 of Qts, 0.5-5,000 litres of Vas, a 0.1-3 target Qtc and a 0.5-5,000 litre net volume; decimal commas are accepted. A target at or below Qts is refused rather than reported as an infinite box, and so is a target that would need more than 5,000 litres. The model is the small-signal one: it ignores box and driver losses (so a real cabinet usually lands slightly flatter), takes the parameters as constant with level, and does not model cone excursion, power handling, port or passive radiator tuning, stuffing placement, a crossover or the room. It runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
